projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: Steve slept only 2.09h last night. May be a rough morning — heads up.

The device count stabilizing at 21-22 after midnight, paired with zero camera motion, confirms the household is fully settled and asleep; the absence of new connections or fluctuations rules out late-night activity or unauthorized access.

The steady increase in connected devices (19 to 22) combined with zero camera motion at 1:05 AM Saturday indicates the family is still awake and settled in for a quiet late night, likely spread across different rooms or watching media. This confirms normal weekend activity and suggests automations should defer night-mode or security triggers.

The steady increase in connected devices (19 to 22) paired with zero camera motion from Friday evening into Saturday early morning indicates a quiet gathering or sleepover where guests are stationary in camera-blind areas, consistent with typical weekend social activity.

The sustained 19–21 device count paired with zero camera activity late on a Friday strongly indicates the household is away (e.g., dining out or at an event) while their devices remain connected to the home network. This warrants a quick verification to ensure no one is home unattended and to confirm security/energy settings are appropriate for an empty house.

The sustained 19–20 device count combined with zero camera motion for over three hours on a Friday evening strongly indicates the home is likely unoccupied or all occupants are in blind spots, suggesting a need to verify occupancy status or investigate a potential network reporting anomaly.

The sustained connection of 19-20 mobile devices paired with zero camera motion on a Friday evening strongly suggests unregistered guests or a gathering inside the home, as the network load far exceeds the household size while the lack of visual activity indicates they are likely confined to a camera-blind area.

The sustained connection of 19-20 mobile devices far exceeds the household's capacity, and combined with zero camera motion over the last 3.5 hours, strongly suggests unauthorized Wi-Fi access or a network reporting anomaly rather than normal occupancy. Steve should verify his Wi-Fi network status and check for unknown devices to rule out unauthorized access.

The sustained 19-20 device count paired with zero camera motion on a Friday evening strongly indicates a large group of guests is gathered inside, likely occupying camera-blind areas or remaining still. This explains the unusual network load and confirms the home is actively occupied despite no motion alerts.

The sustained ~20 device count paired with zero camera motion on a Friday evening strongly indicates the home is unoccupied or the cameras are offline, rather than a normal gathering, warranting a quick security and system check.
